title: cairn-checks-the-floor-before-it-resolves
owner: codemother owns the care of this seam (ruling 2026-09-06); CC/Opus builds. The venv lay-down and the db start each keep their one existing address; bin/cairn calls them.
intention: The `cairn` command checks the floor before it resolves anything: the venv exists, the db is reachable, the instance is set up — and lays what is missing rather than failing into a device that cannot run.
why: Akien's launch chain, told for the second time 2026-09-06 and recorded verbatim at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md. Cast the same day so the intention carries a ticket (CLAUDE.md: an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect).
traces_to: Law 1 (the floor is settled once, by the command, not re-derived by every device) and Law 7 (a missing floor is loud at the one surface the operator is looking at). Akien 2026-09-06 verbatim: 'the cairn command sees that the venv exists, and the db, and that it's all set up' — and 'everything automatically lazy inits'.

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate — bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py (new, beside bin/cairn): isolated HOME, three fault injections each answered in one invocation, happy-path timing recorded. Feeds back naming the check that failed. Durability: committed in cairn; tester seal.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when: (1) with the venv renamed away, `cairn librarian show status` lays a venv and then answers, in one invocation; (2) with the db stopped, the same command starts it and answers; (3) on the happy path the preflight adds under 10ms to bin/cairn's time-to-exec (measure n=15 interleaved, the launchers charter's method); (4) `grep -n venv bin/cairn` is no longer empty (it is empty today, measured 2026-09-06). WRONG INTENT if the preflight grows a second copy of the venv lay-down or the db start — those live in one place each and the command calls them.

questions.a: Two named. (1) 'The db' is the local Postgres on 5432 and starting it is within the user's reach via sudo-relay — standing on this host; phrased as reachability with 'start' as the local remedy so a second host of the instance is not foreclosed. (2) The superclaude launcher's venv preflight can be lifted into a shared function rather than copied — standing; it is a shell block today and becomes bin/cairn's, with the launcher calling it. Neither is load-bearing beyond the build.

One point was asserted wrapped and was not: what 'it's all set up' means concretely. Now wrapped as: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/ exists with flags/ and the instance homes the resolver symlinks into (~/.cairn/devices/<device>/0/bin/). The preflight lays that shape from class-space when missing, using the existing instance setup path, and refuses (loud, nonzero, named) if it cannot.

Consulted the lab. launchers charter's preflight has the same why (floor before anything runs); this widens its reach to the command every caller shares — a distinction to record, and the launcher keeps its own until the command's is proven. Ruling 2026-08-11 (no system-level startup) is honoured: everything here is a lazy lay-down at command time. No Law collides; Law 7 is served.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) the three checks in order and their remedies — venv: `~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3` exists else call the launcher's lay-down; db: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432` (or db_domain's probe if one exists — check cairn/devices/db_domain first) else the store's start path; instance: `~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/` exists else the instance setup; (b) that bin/cairn is bash and must exec the device launcher at the end unchanged; (c) the measurement harness — copy the launchers charter's interleaved n=15 method, report median with min/max, and keep the number in the charter without a gate; (d) don't — no python startup on the happy path (that alone is ~30ms), no daemon, no cache file that could go stale. All written into the ticket's how.

constraints: No change to the ground loop's contents: pulse, control flags, devices-found list — ever (Akien 2026-09-06).
One pipe: device → IPC → own shim → bus → addressee's shim → IPC → addressee; the db alone is exempt (volume).
how: bin/cairn gains a preflight before the device resolver: (1) ~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3 exists, else run the existing venv lay-down (the superclaude launcher already has a preflight that lays the venv — lift that, don't copy it); (2) the db answers on 5432 via db_domain's own probe, else start it the way the store's own tooling does; (3) ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/ exists with the instance shape, else run the instance setup. Each check is a cheap read on the happy path (measured budget: the whole cairn command must stay under the launcher's 76ms median to exec). A failed lay-down is loud and exits nonzero with the check named; it never falls through into the resolver.
links: launchers charter (cairn/launchers/) — the venv preflight to lift, and the measurement method
watchme: none, because the floor is checked on every command by construction; the only operational signal is the happy-path cost, which the proof records and the launchers charter's what_a_launch_COSTS entry (cairn/launchers/intention+why.json) is the precedent for keeping without a gate

intent.what: The `cairn` command checks the floor before it resolves anything: the venv exists, the db is reachable, the instance is set up — and lays what is missing rather than failing into a device that cannot run.

challenge.better_approach: Leaving the floor to the superclaude launcher (which already lays the venv for a CC session) was the status quo; it means `cairn` typed in a bare shell, or by aider, or by codemother, gets no floor. The command is the one entry every caller shares, so the check belongs there. A separate `cairn setup` verb was the other candidate; it survives as the thing the preflight CALLS, not as a step the operator must remember (Law 1).
challenge.prior_art: launchers/superclaude preflight (venv floor, measured to exec) — lift it. db_domain's connect probe and the store's start path. The instance shape under ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<n>/ is already the addressing rule in CLAUDE.md. Nothing in the field to graft; this is a preflight.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That 'the db' means the local Postgres on 5432 and that starting it is something the user manager may do without sudo — true on this host today via sudo-relay; on a second host of the same instance the db is the master elsewhere and 'reachable' replaces 'started'. The check must be phrased as reachability, with 'start' as the local remedy.
challenge.real_collision: None found. The launchers charter's preflight has the same why (the floor is laid before anything runs); this generalizes its reach from one launcher to the command every launcher shares. Distinction to record: the launcher keeps its own preflight until the command's is proven, then calls the command's.

decisions.text: the cairn command sees that the venv exists, and the db, and that it's all set up. it also sees that the librarian is a device (there's a resolver in cairn) and so goes to cairn/cairn/librarian/bin/librarian and passes in 'show status hot'.

WHERE: one bash function `_floor` in bin/cairn, called ONCE, after the no-argument first-run branch (bin/cairn:58-74, which already hands a bare `cairn` to launchers/bootstrap_first_run.sh) and before `device="${1,,}"` (bin/cairn:79) — so every dispatched command crosses it and the resolver never runs on a floor that is not laid. bin/cairn stays bash and still ends in `exec "$target" "$@"` unchanged. MEASURED AT cairn commit 09475560 (2026-09-16, `git show 09475560 --stat`: bin/cairn, bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py, launchers/bootstrap.sh, launchers/bootstrap_first_run.sh): the no-argument first-run branch is bin/cairn:59-74 (its bootstrap call at :65), the floor block is bin/cairn:86-146 (`_floor` called once at :146), and the device assignment `device="${1,,}"; shift` is bin/cairn:151 — so the floor runs after the no-arg branch and before the first token is read, as this line says.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 2: line numbers re-measured against the committed bin/cairn (09475560): first-run branch 59-74, floor 86-146, device assignment 151

decisions.text: `HERE` IS ALREADY DEFINED at bin/cairn:28, file scope, before everything below: `HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")" && pwd)"` — the dispatcher's own directory, symlinks resolved, so `$HERE/../launchers/bootstrap.sh` is the repo's launchers/bootstrap.sh whichever path `cairn` was reached by. The floor adds nothing to it and defines no HERE of its own. VARIABLES FIRST, at file scope of bin/cairn, before `_floor` is defined: `INSTANCE_ROOT` already exists (bin/cairn:26 `INSTANCE_ROOT="${CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cairn/devices}"`); the floor adds two beside it, `CAIRN_VENV="${CAIRN_VENV:-$HOME/.cairn/venv}"` and `CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR="${CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR:-/var/run/postgresql}"`, and every test and every lay-down below reads those three names and no other. THE HAPPY PATH IS THREE BASH BUILTIN TESTS AND NOTHING ELSE — no subprocess, no python, no cache file: (1) `[[ -x "${CAIRN_VENV:-$HOME/.cairn/venv}/bin/python3" ]]` (the path bootstrap.sh:92 `cairn_venv_dir` resolves, so the check and the lay-down agree on the address); (2) `[[ -S "${CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR:-/var/run/postgresql}/.s.PGSQL.5432" ]]` — the unix socket db_domain itself connects through (store.py:57 `SOCKET_DIR = "/var/run/postgresql"`, store.py:79/94 `psycopg2.connect(host=SOCKET_DIR, …)`), so the cheap read is the door's own route and not a proxy for it; (3) `[[ -d "$INSTANCE_ROOT/cairn/0" ]]` — the cairn device's instance home, under which the ground loop's liveness record, the sail record and last_known.json live (measured: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/{bin,last_known.json,machines,tools}). BASELINE MEASURED 2026-09-16: bin/cairn reaches exit against a stand-in device (`exit 0` verb under a scratch CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT) in 4.3ms median, n=15, min 4.1 max 4.7, load 2.5 — the falsifier's clause (3) budget is <10ms added, and three builtin tests are microseconds. MEASURED AT cairn commit 09475560 (2026-09-16, `git show 09475560 --stat`: bin/cairn, bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py, launchers/bootstrap.sh, launchers/bootstrap_first_run.sh): `INSTANCE_ROOT` bin/cairn:26, `HERE` :28, `CAIRN_VENV` :86, `CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR` :87.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 2: HERE named as pre-existing at bin/cairn:28 (the rehearsal's one unlisted step); the four file-scope names re-measured at 09475560

decisions.text: THE VENV LAY-DOWN IS LIFTED, NOT COPIED: on a miss of test (1), bin/cairn sources `$HERE/../launchers/bootstrap.sh` — NOTHING IS EXTRACTED FROM ANYWHERE: `cairn_bootstrap_verify` (bootstrap.sh:123) and `cairn_bootstrap_apply` (bootstrap.sh:178) ALREADY EXIST in that sourceable file today, measured 2026-09-16 (`grep -n '^cairn_bootstrap_' launchers/bootstrap.sh` → 123, 178, 238); superclaude:186-191 is merely their first CALLER, and bin/cairn becomes the second caller of the same two functions and calls `cairn_bootstrap_verify >/dev/null 2>&1 || cairn_bootstrap_apply >/dev/null 2>&1`; if verify still fails after apply, print `cairn: floor: venv — ` + each line of CAIRN_BOOTSTRAP_FINDINGS to stderr and `exit 3`. No second venv recipe exists anywhere in bin/cairn (WRONG INTENT clause; `grep -c 'python3 -m venv' bin/cairn` is 0). The heavy path is only ever paid on a miss (Law 1: the settled floor is not re-derived per launch). The venv address is `$CAIRN_VENV` (D3) throughout — bootstrap.sh's `cairn_venv_dir` (bootstrap.sh:92) returns `${CAIRN_VENV:-$HOME/.cairn/venv}`, the same default, so the test, the lay-down and D5's PATH export name one directory. MEASURED AT cairn commit 09475560 (2026-09-16, `git show 09475560 --stat`: bin/cairn, bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py, launchers/bootstrap.sh, launchers/bootstrap_first_run.sh): `grep -n '^cairn_' launchers/bootstrap.sh` → cairn_venv_dir 92, cairn_python 96, cairn_bootstrap_verify 123, cairn_bootstrap_apply 178, cairn_bootstrap_report 238, cairn_wire_instances 293 — the addresses this line cites are the committed ones.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 2: verify/apply addresses re-measured at the commit (123/178), the whole function roster listed

decisions.text: THE VENV IS USED, NOT ONLY SEEN: after test (1) passes or the lay-down lands, `export PATH="$CAIRN_VENV/bin:$PATH"` (CAIRN_VENV from D3, file scope — no function-local variable crosses between the checks) (superclaude:196-197's two lines) so the device launcher's `python3` IS the floor — today every launcher is `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `exec python3 …` (cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin/cairn:4), so `cairn <device>` runs under whichever python3 is first on PATH. Measured 2026-09-16: a CC session already runs with the venv first (`which python3` → ~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3), so this changes nothing for CC-launched commands and makes Akien's terminal commands run the same interpreter.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 1: $venv → $CAIRN_VENV (D3's file-scope name)

decisions.text: THE DB PROBE ON A MISS of test (2) is `pg_isready -h "$sockdir" -p 5432 -q` (a real round trip, only paid when the socket file is absent — a socket file can outlive a crashed server, so the miss path re-asks with the real question); if it answers, the floor is up and nothing is started. If not, the start is ONE call, `sudo -n systemctl start postgresql.service` (measured: this box runs the debian cluster `postgresql@16-main.service`, started through the umbrella `postgresql.service`; there is NO start tooling in cairn/devices/db_domain — `grep -rn 'pg_ctl\|systemctl' cairn/devices/db_domain/*.py` is empty — so this call is the one place the db is started from, and the store's own connect() (store.py:90) then finds it). After a start that returned 0, poll THE SOCKET FILE (`[[ -S "$CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR/.s.PGSQL.5432" ]]`, the same path test (2) reads) — `sleep 0.2` between attempts, 75 attempts, 15s in all; the first hit returns 0. The 75th miss → `cairn: floor: db — postgres was started (systemctl start postgresql.service returned 0) but <socket> did not appear within 15s`, exit 3. A start that returned non-zero never reaches the poll: `cairn: floor: db — postgres is down at <socket> and this user could not start it (sudo -n systemctl start postgresql.service: <sudo's own words, or 'refused' if it said nothing>); lay the sudoers line once — the ollama line's twin, for /bin/systemctl start postgresql.service — or run: cairn sudorelay`, exit 3. `pg_isready` is asked exactly once, before the start, on the socket-file miss, and always on `-h "$CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR" -p 5432` (the D3 variable, default /var/run/postgresql) — measured at cairn 09475560, bin/cairn:106-123 (`_floor_db`).
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 3: the poll stated as the code runs it: socket file, 75 x 0.2s, after a zero-rc start only; pg_isready once on the miss, on $CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR; both refusal texts verbatim

decisions.text: ROOT IS NOT ASSUMED: `sudo -n` never prompts. Measured 2026-09-16: `sudo -n -l` on this box permits NOPASSWD only `/bin/systemctl start|restart ollama.service`; the sudo_relay daemon (cairn/devices/sudo_relay, `cairn sudorelay`) is not running. So today a down db reads as `cairn: floor: db — … sudo: a password is required — lay the sudoers line once (the ollama line's twin, for `/bin/systemctl start postgresql.service`) or run `cairn sudorelay`` and exits 3, loud and named — which is the falsifier's 'never falls through into the resolver'. Whether that sudoers line is laid on this box is Akien's (a root-laid host-seam) — question open-f4c0d8bc4f94 (opened at cast); the build does not wait on it because the code path is the same either way; only the live fire's clause (2) reading does.

THE INSTANCE LAY-DOWN IS LIFTED TOO — BUILT AND MEASURED 2026-09-16: bootstrap_first_run.sh's step 3 (its two functions `_wire_device`, `_wire_single` and the class-space scan, formerly lines 66-115) now lives in launchers/bootstrap.sh as `cairn_wire_instances` (appended after `cairn_bootstrap_report`; same bodies, the two helpers nested inside it, `instance_root="${CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cairn/devices}"` read at call time, counts printed as `wired N skipped M`, returns 0 always — bootstrap.sh's no-set-e rule holds). bootstrap_first_run.sh's step 3 is now the one call `CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT="$INSTANCE_ROOT" cairn_wire_instances` (bootstrap.sh is already sourced at its step 1, line 28). Measured against a scratch root: `wired 7 skipped 0` → cc codemother inference_domain librarian superclaude tester trouble, each bin a symlink into class-space (e.g. tester/0/bin/tester → cairn/devices/tester/0/bin/tester) — the same result the old inline loop produced. bin/cairn calls the same function on a miss of test (3), then `mkdir -p "$INSTANCE_ROOT/cairn/0"` (class-space has no cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin to wire from — measured `ls -d cairn/devices/*/0/bin` lists cc, codemother, inference_domain, librarian, tester, trouble — so the cairn device's instance home is made here, the way its machines would make it on first write). A still-missing `$INSTANCE_ROOT/cairn/0` after that → `cairn: floor: instance — <path> could not be laid` to stderr, `exit 3`. MEASURED AT cairn commit 09475560 (2026-09-16, `git show 09475560 --stat`: bin/cairn, bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py, launchers/bootstrap.sh, launchers/bootstrap_first_run.sh): `cairn_wire_instances` is launchers/bootstrap.sh:293 and bootstrap_first_run.sh's step 3 is the one call `CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT="$INSTANCE_ROOT" cairn_wire_instances` guarded by `declare -F cairn_wire_instances`; bin/cairn's `_floor_instance` (:125-138) sources bootstrap.sh and calls it on a miss. The proof's tooth `test_absent_venv_is_laid_then_answers` and its `_probe_device` scratch root exercise the miss branch under a scratch CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT; the resting tooth measures that a present root is not touched.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 2: cairn_wire_instances address re-measured at the commit (bootstrap.sh:293); the caller in bin/cairn and the proof teeth that exercise it named

decisions.text: THE FOUR REFUSALS SHARE ONE SHAPE: `cairn: floor: <venv|db|instance> — <what was probed, what came back, the one remedy>` on stderr, exit code 3 (distinct from the resolver's 127 and 2), and the resolver is never reached (the falsifier's 'a failed lay-down is loud and exits nonzero with the check named'). A `--no-floor` flag is NOT added — the launcher's `--no-preflight` is a rescue hatch for a launcher that must never abort; bin/cairn's whole job here is to refuse a floor it cannot lay (gates are physics).

THE PROOF bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py (new, beside bin/cairn; PROVES over the falsifier's four clauses; plain script, no pytest — tester runs proofs via runpy): every tooth runs bin/cairn as a subprocess with HOME=<scratch>, CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT=<scratch>/devices, CAIRN_VENV=<scratch>/venv, and CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR set per tooth. The falsifier's `cairn librarian show status` is today `cairn librarian --status` — the librarian launcher's status face (cairn/devices/librarian/0/bin/librarian:37-44: prints whether port 80 listens, exits 0/1, spawns nothing); `show status` is the standard vocabulary (ticket 15d6a0ef9c11) not yet on that launcher — so the proof drives `--status`, and 'answers' means the launcher's own status line printed and its own exit code (0 or 1) returned. Teeth: (1) venv absent → one invocation lays a venv at CAIRN_VENV (pip install -e, measured ~20-60s) AND prints the librarian's status line; (2) db: CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR=<scratch>/nosock (no socket) → the invocation refuses with `cairn: floor: db —` and exit 3 and the librarian launcher NEVER ran (its status line absent) — the sudo-refused branch, which is what this user gets today; the started branch is the live fire's reading, not the proof's (a proof cannot stop root's postgres); (3) happy path timing: n=15 interleaved, bin/cairn HEAD~ vs bin/cairn now, against the stand-in `exit 0` verb, median delta < 10ms, both medians printed; (4) `grep -n venv bin/cairn` non-empty. Plus a resting tooth: with all three present, no lay-down runs (bootstrap.sh is not sourced: measured by CAIRN_VENV pointing at a dir holding only bin/python3 as an executable stub, which a verify would refuse and an apply would rebuild — the stub is intact after the run). MEASURED 2026-09-16 (cairn/devices/librarian/0/bin/librarian, unchanged by this ticket): the `--status` flag is the file's own documented usage (:15 `cairn librarian --status  just report whether it's up`), tested at :35 `if [[ "${1:-}" == "--status" ]]`, and the interactive-browser branch at :173-174 explicitly excludes it; it prints the status line and exits 0 (listening) or 1 (not) and spawns nothing. It is the one librarian verb that is safe to fire inside a proof today, which is why the proof drives it; if a later ticket changes that flag the proof's stand-in tooth reds, which is the right reading.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 2: librarian --status measured in the launcher (:15 usage, :35 test, :173-174 exclusion), stated as the reason the proof drives it

decisions.text: THE LIVE FIRE: `cairn tester` from a terminal on this box with the floor up — the three tests pass, the launcher's python3 is the venv's, time-to-exec measured n=15 against the baseline. Clause (2)'s started-branch reading (db stopped → `cairn` starts it) is taken ONLY if Akien lays the sudoers line (open question); otherwise the refused branch is the recorded reading and clause (2) stands as the falsifier's sudo-refused half — written into the ticket as a measurement before PROVEME either way. THE READING TAKEN TODAY, 2026-09-16, floor up: `cairn tester` rc 0 in 64ms, python3 from $CAIRN_VENV, n=15 delta +0.1ms (5.3ms vs 5.2ms at HEAD's dispatcher) — the proof's clause (3). Clause (2) today: with CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR pointed at an empty dir, `cairn: floor: db — postgres is down at <dir>/.s.PGSQL.5432 and this user could not start it (sudo -n systemctl start postgresql.service: sudo: a password is required); lay the sudoers line once …`, rc 3, nothing resolved — the REFUSED branch, and it is the reading this ticket ships on. The ORDER IS SETTLED HERE, not by the question: the ticket does not wait for the sudoers line; open-f4c0d8bc4f94 asks Akien whether to lay it, and if he does, the started-branch reading (db stopped → `cairn` starts it → socket within 15s) is taken then and appended to this line as a second measurement. If he does not, the refused branch stays the only live reading and the started branch is covered by the code path alone (identical lines either way, bin/cairn:115-122). The question blocks PROVEME only because every open question does (buildme_has_no_open_questions), not because the build depends on the answer.
decisions.amended: 2026-09-16 by CC after rehearsal pass 3: today's readings written in (refused branch, rc 3; happy path 64ms, +0.1ms); the ticket ships on the refused branch, the started-branch reading is appended only if the sudoers line is laid

decisions.text: NEVER: no python startup on the happy path (~30ms alone — the builder_check's own number); no daemon, no poller, no cache file that can go stale; no second copy of the venv recipe or the wiring loop (both are lifted into bootstrap.sh and called from two places); bin/cairn never starts the ground loop, the web server or any device — those are the shim's (d6eb399ab6ad) and the launchers' — the floor is venv + db + instance dir and nothing more.

SEAL: run twice green bare, then `cairn test --hollow 0853294fe972 --seal` under the tester; the PROVEME crossing names bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py in proven_by. WATCH: none — the ticket's cast watchme stands (the floor is checked on every command by construction).

D1 is Akien's intent verbatim and carries no how; the how is D2-D13 in order — the venv lay-down is D4, the db probe-and-start is D6, the instance lay-down is D8, the refusal shape D9, the proof D10, the live fire D11. A builder reads the lines in sequence; D1 alone builds nothing.

CAIRN_VENV and CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR are FILE-SCOPE statements at bin/cairn:86-87, outside every function: _floor_refuse is defined at :89, _floor_venv :94, _floor_db :106, _floor_instance :125, and _floor itself at :140-145, called once at :146 — the two assignments stand 53 lines ABOVE the function they serve, measured at cairn 09475560 with grep -n '_floor\|^CAIRN_' bin/cairn.
